title: Tests wait on events, not clocks: remove the poll loops and guessed deadlines
description:
Mark 2026-11-27: "i dont like hardcoding and i dont like poll loops and
i dont like sleep(n) then do loops" and "we spent 50 years putting
events in *nix. use it".

## Why it is not just taste

binary_smoke.rs waited for a startup line with
`while !logs().contains(line) { sleep(1ms) }` and two hardcoded 30s
deadlines. Converted to `tokio::process` (epoll on the pipes, SIGCHLD
through `Child::wait`) with `select!` on "a line arrived" against "the
process exited":

- the test that failed at 30.38s now runs in 12-26s, 3 of 3
- the whole file went from 102.63s to 12.47s
- both deadlines are gone, not raised

So the poll loop was the cost, not the machine. That also undercuts the
PATIENCE knob added the same day (commit 31da066c): it treated a
symptom.

## The primitives, now in place

- `common::until_store(store, ready)` in the agent harness: waits on
  `Store::subscribe`, the broadcast of published sequence numbers the
  front ends already follow. No sleep, no deadline.
- `PushControl::until` waits on a Notify the request layer fires, not a
  20ms poll.

## Done

binary_smoke.rs entirely; the agent harness primitives; irc.rs
(until_gone and the room-record wait), irc_two_providers.rs.

## Left, by kind

1. `while <condition> { sleep }` over store state. Mechanical with
   until_store. About 20 sites: didwebvh_log, jmap_seed, disappearing,
   groundwork, push, direct_two_providers, jmap_off, irc_v2 in
   mimid-agent, plus hub_acceptance, hub_update, follower_e2e,
   two_provider_catchup, jmap_two_providers, mtls_binaries,
   common/providers in mimid-server, and expiry/calls in
   mimid-agent-store.
2. Bare `sleep(n)` then assert, with no loop. Harder and more
   interesting: several assert a NEGATIVE ("nothing arrived"), where
   there is no event to await by construction, so the sleep is standing
   in for "long enough that it would have". Those need a different
   technique per case -- usually making the thing that would have
   happened observable, then asserting the count did not move -- not a
   longer sleep. Sites include push.rs:150, front_end_auth.rs:666,
   no_token_in_logs.rs:215, irc_v2.rs:586 and :869, groundwork.rs:494.

mimid-server's tests need the equivalent of until_store against its own
store; check whether it publishes a change signal before writing one.

## Not to change

Production sleeps are backoffs, rate-limit delays, grace periods, and
periodic maintenance already in `select!` with event arms: register.rs,
http.rs, client.rs, stream.rs, runner.rs, daemon.rs, push.rs,
fanout.rs, main.rs. A timer is the right tool for "every N"; none of
these polls for an event that could be signalled.
notes: 2026-11-27: the sweep is done across the test harnesses. PATIENCE and MIMID_TEST_PATIENCE_SECS are gone, with the CI env var. Converted: mimid-agent (13 files), mimid-agent-core (12), mimid-agent-store (8, with a new tests/common/mod.rs holding the shared change signal), mimid-agent-jmap (9, same), mimid-server (10). Four production observables were added to make it possible, each useful outside the tests: PushSubscriptions::changed (mimid-agent-store), FanoutHandle::passed and Hub::fanout (mimid-server), Follower::subscribe_positions and Follower::appended_sender (mimid-server), and Daemon::push_subscriptions (mimid-agent). The rule the conversions follow: a poll or sync that read something is repeated at once, because one change at the server can take an agent several of them; one that read nothing waits for a real event. Five waits remain, each with a comment saying why: three bounded negatives (jmap_projection bob's quiet stream, irc_v2 no push after unregister, front_end_auth the per-source connection count), and two blocked on bead mimid-67e0.2 (binary_smoke's in-flight request, mtls_binaries' cross-process Jmap::next). Wall-clock waits that remain are single sleeps to a deadline, not loops: a message expiry, a retention window, a credential recheck.
